reason: Runnable (gp factormod + python int bit-vectors, well under 20 CPU-min; metric is counts/fractions, not wall time). Three defects as written. (a) The headline test 'bit-for-bit agreement of convolution identity with CRT predicate (P)&(F)&(Sh)' is a ring-isomorphism tautology (F_2[X]/(X^N-1) = F_2 x F_{2^n} x F_{2^n}); it can only fail through a coding bug, so it is a unit test, not a discriminator. The only non-tautological content is the lift-count prediction (0 for w=2 / L1, ~1/2 for L2 w=3). (b) No null arm: nothing shows the test can fail, i.e. no control where the CRT predicate is expected to disagree or where a hidden x->xbar/group-law correlation would be detected. (c) Power: at n=23, w=3, 64 targets the expected number of field solutions of S_3=0 is ~ (16215 x 64)/2^22 ~ 0.25 (S_3 is quadratic, ~2 roots per ~2^n), so the 0.50+-0.05 co-lift fraction is untestable there; at n=11 expected ~ 1771x256/2^10 ~ 440 solutions, sigma ~0.024, so +-0.05 is only ~2 sigma (false-alarm ~5%). Also underspecified: the lift of the curve constant a6 (prediction 'S_3(0,0,e)=1 so even weight gives 0' holds only if parity(a6 lift)=1; for random a6 it is a free choice and the even-weight zero result then fails), definition of 'gamma-weight' pairs for w=3, and why L1 (c_i=c_{-i}) gives exactly 0 (the shadow component then equals the field component, so the zero must come from the parity/a6 side; needs to be derived, not assumed). Scaling: toy says nothing about n=131 except through the proof (CRT dims 1,n,n are exact for any N=2n+1 prime with ord_N(2)=n); that is acceptable for a negative theory item but the verdict 'N1 closed' only covers lifts L1, L2, not the sparse canonical lift flagged in risk. Wall bypassed is not claimed (theory closure), so no non-genericity certificate issue.
fix: 1) Demote bit-for-bit CRT agreement to a code self-check; state it as such. 2) Make the discriminating test the lift-count law: for each n in {11,23}, enumerate/sample pairs (x1,x2) of sparse elements (w=2: all C(N,2); w=3: all at n=11, 2e5 random weight-3 pairs at n=23), and instead of random targets SOLVE for x_R: S_3(x1,x2,X)=0 is quadratic in X over F_{2^n} (half-trace / gp polrootsmod-style or direct Artin-Schreier), giving ~5e4 planted field solutions at n=23 and ~1e5+ at n=11. Then count exact group-algebra lifts via brute force over the kernel freedom of x_R's lift (2^(1+n) kernel elements at n=11 is 4096, fine; at n=23 use the linear-algebra parameterisation: parity bit and shadow component are affine in kernel coordinates, so exact-lift existence = solving for (parity, shadow) = target values, test by direct evaluation of the convolution identity in F_2[X]/(X^N-1) on a sample of 2000 solutions). 3) Report fraction with exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CI and pre-register the pass band as CI containing 0.5 and the co-lift fraction computed independently from (P),(Sh) coin; require N_solutions >= 2000 per cell. 4) Null arms: (i) wrong-ring null: relabel exponents by a random non-automorphism permutation of Z/N (breaks the ring hom) and show the CRT predicate disagrees with the convolution identity at rate ~50% (shows test can fail); (ii) shuffled-coin null: pair each solution's (P,Sh) values with a random other solution and show co-lift fraction is unchanged iff the coin is curve/solution independent; (iii) curve-variation arm: repeat for 8 random a6 (and a6=1) with a6 lifts of both parities, confirming the even-weight zero result holds only for parity(a6 lift)=1 and report the rule. 5) Add lift L3 = minimum-weight/sparse canonical preimage of x_R (the risk case) and report its exact-lift fraction; if it differs from 1/2 beyond CI, flag N1 as not closed for that lift. 6) Cheap scaling sanity: gp factormod(X^N-1,2) degrees for N=23,47,167,263 (n=11,23,83,131) confirming (1,n,n) and that f* != f; no need to run the lift count at n=131. 7) Metrics: counts of solutions, exact lifts, CI, rank of kernel->(parity,shadow) map (expect full rank 2 on n>=11); no timing. Budget ~3-6 CPU-min.
